problem.h: They’ve already got a rollercoaster in their head
p: Children who love theme parks are always dreaming up the next ride: a loop round a volcano, a ghost train run by real ghosts. Most of it never leaves their head.
A blank notebook doesn’t show them how a whole park comes together, so the idea fizzles out.

approach.h: Fifteen pages, from first sketch to opening day
p: The book takes young designers through six complete theme parks. Each one goes from the first ride sketch all the way to opening day, fifteen pages at a time.
A “Stuck for an idea?” prompt waits at the start of every park, and there’s a list of 100 park ideas at the back. The rest is up to them.

offer.p: Big A4 pages with room for every loop, map and mascot.
features: Maps, rollercoasters, rides and mascots, fifteen pages per park.
Ten short lessons on maps, how rollercoasters work, rides, mascots and happy visitors.
A dice game for every park: roll for each hour and see how many visitors come through the gates.
